newsitem.title: INDIA: India IDBI cuts prime rate to 15.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: India IDBI cuts prime rate to 15.0 pct.

text.p: The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) said on Monday it will cut its minimum term lending rate to 15.0 percent per annum from 16.5 percent, with effect from May 1.
The maximum spread in the rate of interest is set at 3.5 percentage points over the prime rate, depending on the risk perception, the bank said in a statement.
The revised rate is exclusive of interest tax.
The cut in rates follows the easier monetary and credit policy for first half 1997/98 (April-March) announced by the Reserve Bank of India on April 15, IDBI said.

"Following the announcement of the slack season credit policy, there has been downward movement in interest rates," it said. "IDBI's cost of funds during the current year (1997/98) is expected to be significantly lower."
Sanctions during 1996/97 totalled 163.53 billion rupees, a 4.6 percent decline over the previous year, IDBI said.
Loan disbursals grew 6.0 percent to 112.76 billion rupees in the same period, it said.
The bank borrowed 98.03 billion rupees in rupee loans and the equivalent of $582 million in foreign currency during 1996/97, the statement said.

The foreign currency borrowings include a floating rate note issue of $150 million, syndicated/club loans of $250 million, bilateral loans of $50 million and DM50 million and a line of credit of $50 million.
IDBI is India's leading term lending bank.
The rate cut announced by IDBI is the first among term lenders and bankers said it was an indication of long-term interest rates coming down.
Following the credit policy announcement earlier this month, several leading state-run and foreign banks announced cuts in their prime lending rates ranging from 50 to 150 basis points.
